questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me to choose a place that I hadn't visited before, and also that the school had courses that could be transferred to my home university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Only negative thing was the expensive rent and the distance to the school.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was kind of confusing in the beginning. Netpa and the sharepoint were very hard to figure out and I still really haven't. But you figure everything out as you go.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't participate in the welcome week, so I didn't receive assistance per se, but I went to the student counsil a lot of times, because of trouble with enrollment.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very hard. I lived with two friends from home, and we were lucky to get an apartment through someone we knew, but when we didn't know that we could rent that apartment, we tried Facebook groups, but it felt too sketchy. We also looked at a lot of different housing website. My most important advice is too start looking early, because when we tried to find something a couple of months before we had to leave, it was impossible.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be very expensive. It's a good idea to check if you live near a train station or metro if you wanna take public transportation to school. The busses (and also the trains) are very unreliable.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was so confusing. They had a lot of confusing and contradictory information on the different platforms (website and sharepoint documents). They changed the ECTS points on the courses from 7,5 to 7, but it only said so sometimes. The enrollment was very stressful, and because I needed some specific courses to be able to obtain 30 ECTS it was crucial for me that the website worked, but it didn't. Sometimes some courses weren't showing. My friend and I also applied for the exact same courses at the exact same time, but he ended up getting completely different courses than me - random courses that he couldn't use, so we have spend so many hours at the student counsil trying to fix this, but they were no help. After around 1,5 months we finally fixed the problem by getting our home university to contact the professor at Nova, that had the course he couldn't enroll in (because it wasn't showing on the website in the post-enrollment period), and he luckily ended up getting the course. But we had to come up with this solution ourselves. I think if it was me this happened to, I would have wished that I would just have stayed home in Denmark, which sound very dramatic, but it was so stressful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The student council, but they didn't really help with this, because they couldn't fix the technical problems.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the courses that I wanted, but had to take 6 different courses to obtain 30 ECTS: 3 courses of 7 ECTS and 3 of 3,5.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Decide before the enrollment period start which courses you want. The student council is very hard to get ahold of by email, so go to the student council on campus if you have trouble with anything.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level were maybe a little bit easier than home in some courses, but not all.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The final grade is composed of different tests, midterms, assignments, attendance, presentations, and the final exam. I liked this so that the final exam didn't count for 100 percent like at home. In practical classes it was only the teacher doing the exercises. At UCPH the students usually do exercises themselves and then ask the teacher for help.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Advanced Microeconomics, Industrial Organization, Development Economics, Introduction to Modern and Contemporary History, Economic History, Law in Business and Economics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed all of my courses, except Development Economics, which was very boring, the teacher was hard to understand because of a french accent, and there was a lot of work (big assignment, presentation and lots of texts to read).

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Used Uber and Bolt all the time.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transportation was cheap, rent was expensive, food in supermarkets only a little cheaper than in Denmark, but much cheaper to go to restaurants, bars, cafés, clubs etc.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't really use them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Surfing, some school parties, other kinds of clubs - but again I didn't use them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I don't know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out for all meals, go to museums (loved MAAT), just go sit in the parks and drink cheap coffee/beer at the Quiosque or go to one of the many Miradouro, where there also always is a Quiosque. Also go to markets on saturdays.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was easy enough.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Many locals are very bad at English, which can be troublesome in shops, supermarkets etc.
The locals appreciate if you pay in cash - also in supermarkets.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
People were very friendly and chill - more relaxed vibe compared to Denmark.
People were outside a lot.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Check up beforehand on which courses you want.
Buy a monthly travel card (50 euro each month).
Use the student council at school - they are very nice.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There is a canteen, where you can buy lunch for 3 euro, which I think saves a lot of time and is cheap. There is also a supermarket at school which I also almost used every day. If you like to surf, you can get access to surf lockers, where you can keep your surf board and take showers etc. 
The school is also a really nice place to study - a lot of seating areas.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just being on my own, making new friends and experiencing the Portuguese culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Travel time to school. However, if you are only going for 1 semester, you should definitely stay in Lisbon and not Carcavelos, which is a very boring city. The public transportation is worth it:)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
